Why boring tech wins

By Sam Rivera — March 2026

Every few years the industry rediscovers the same lesson: the systems that survive are the ones nobody has to think about. This post is about choosing boring on purpose.

The cost of novelty

New tools demand attention. Attention is the scarcest resource on any team, and it compounds: every unfamiliar layer multiplies the debugging surface.

Choose the technology you can operate while tired.

A checklist

  • Can two people on the team debug it at 3am?
  • Has it been stable for five years?
  • Does it fail loudly and predictably?

Migration order

  1. Inventory what you run today
  2. Delete what nobody can explain
  3. Replace the rest one piece at a time

None of this is glamorous. That is precisely the point.
